title: Extraction of ß-Carotene from Pumpkin (Curcubita moschata) and Spinach (Spinacia oleracea) Using Environmentally Friendly Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs)
content: There is an increasing demand for antioxidants, nutraceuticals and natural colorants. ß-Carotene is one of the commonly used commodities which fits description. ß-Carotene is a highly hydrophobic molecule; therefore, commercial extraction processes generally use highly non-polar solvents and these are barely environmentally friendly chemicals. The aim of this research was to develop effective and sustainable extraction processes for ß-Carotene from pumpkin and spinach using environmentally friendly green chemicals. A series of deep eutectic solvents with L-menthol and carboxylic aliphatic acids were synthesized for extraction of β-carotene from pumpkin and spinach via mechanical mixing (MMAE) and homogenization assisted extraction (HAE). Response surface methodology and ANOVA analyses were used to analyze the data. Menthol:Propionic Acid DESs had the best effect on the extraction of ß-Carotene (11.528 μg-ß-Carotene/gr-pumpkin for MMAE, 8.966 μg-ß-Carotene/gr-pumpkin for HAE, 16.924 μg-ß-Carotene/gr-spinach for MMAE and 18.870 μg-ß-Carotene/gr-spinach for HAE) under the optimal conditions (HBD molar ratio: 0.6452, 15 min. for MMAE of ß-Carotene from pumpkin, HBD molar ratio: 0.6198, 30.0 sec., 7061 rpm for HAE of ß-Carotene from pumpkin, HBD molar ratio: 0.8000, 60 min. for MMAE of ß-Carotene from spinach, HBD molar ratio: 0.8000, 120.0 sec., 7000 rpm for HAE of ß-Carotene from spinach).
